about: I'm a Computer Science student at Northbridge University. This whole site is demo content — open the admin panel at /admin and replace every word with your own story.
My work sits between machine learning and real products: I like taking an idea from a notebook to something a real person can open on their phone.
Outside of code I read, hike, and help run the university's developer club. Tell visitors what makes you, you — two to four short paragraphs work best.

projects.title: Study Buddy
projects.subtitle: An AI tutor that answers from your own lecture notes
projects.summary: Upload your slides and notes, then ask questions — every answer cites the page it came from.
projects.problem: Students waste hours searching through slides and PDFs. General chatbots answer confidently but can't point to the course material, so students can't trust them.
approach: Split lecture PDFs into sections and indexed them with vector embeddings.
Retrieved the most relevant passages for each question and asked the model to answer only from them, with citations.
Built a simple web app so classmates could try it during exam week.
impact: Answers with citations were rated trustworthy by 9 in 10 testers

projects.title: City Pulse
projects.subtitle: Open data about your city, made readable
projects.summary: A dashboard that turns public transport and air-quality data into simple daily charts.
projects.problem: The city publishes useful open data, but only as large CSV files that almost nobody opens.
approach: Wrote a nightly job that downloads and cleans the data.
Designed a small set of charts that answer everyday questions.
impact: Featured in the local newspaper's tech column

projects.title: Pocket Coach
projects.subtitle: A habit-tracking app with gentle reminders
projects.summary: A small Android app that helps you build one habit at a time.
projects.problem: Most habit apps ask you to track ten things at once, and people give up in a week.
approach: Designed the app around a single habit and a daily check-in.
Used on-device notifications with smart timing.
impact: Beta tested with 30 friends over four weeks
projects.note: Beta — not on the Play Store yet.

projects.title: Signal Lens
projects.subtitle: Reading traffic signs from dash-cam video
projects.summary: A course project that detects and classifies traffic signs in real time.
projects.problem: Detect small signs reliably in low light and motion blur.
approach: Fine-tuned a YOLO model on a public dataset.
impact: 92% mAP on the held-out test set

statement: I'm interested in making AI systems that can show their work — models that cite their sources and admit when they don't know.
My current work looks at how retrieval can make small language models reliable enough for education.

publications.title: Grounded Tutoring: Citing Lecture Material in LLM Answers
publications.abstract: We study how retrieval over course material changes the accuracy and trustworthiness of answers from a language-model tutor. In a study with 120 students, answers that cited lecture pages were rated more trustworthy and were more often correct. (Demo abstract — replace it with your own.)
